answer: Retrospective correlation scoring: each identity's actions are clustered by timing, phrasing, and shared infrastructure; clusters that behave as a garden of near-identical accounts get flagged after the fact. Enforcement is a graduated withdrawal of visibility and payout eligibility across the whole cluster. To survive, an attacker must build genuinely distinct behavior on every island of activity, splitting budgets and pacing across weeks. The dune of cheap throwaway accounts erodes, since each surviving identity now costs sustained, non-repeating effort rather than a one-time fee.
